10

The wrong side of the river

Scroll
Vila Nova de Gaia

The wine crosses
the river

Port isn't made in Porto. It's made eighty kilometres inland, up the Douro, on terraces cut into schist so steep the vines are farmed by hand. Then it comes downriver and stops — on the other bank, in Vila Nova de Gaia, where the lodges have been ageing it in cool dark sheds for three hundred years.

That's the whole trick, and it's geography. Gaia faces north, gets no sun, and sits in the damp coming off the Atlantic. The wine ages slowly there. Cross the bridge to Porto and it would cook.

At the end of this week we cross the Douro and go find out what the fuss is about.

The ritual

How to taste it
without looking lost

Four steps, in order, and none of them are optional if you want the guide to nod at you instead of at the person next to you.

  1. Look

    Tilt the glass against something white. The colour at the rim tells you the age — purple means young, amber means it has been in wood a long time.

  2. Swirl

    Once, slowly, on the table. You're pushing air into it. The streaks that run back down the glass are the "legs", and thick slow ones mean sugar and alcohol.

  3. Smell

    Nose in, mouth slightly open, two short sniffs. This is most of what you think tasting is. The tongue only does five things; the nose does the rest.

  4. Sip

    Small. Hold it. Port is roughly twenty percent alcohol because they stop the fermentation with grape spirit while the sugar is still in there — that's why it's sweet and why it hits.

The flight

Six glasses,
lightest first

A tasting runs in one direction: pale and cold at the start, dark and sweet at the end, because anything heavy ruins whatever follows it. This is the order we're ordering in.

01

White

Branco Chilled, 8 °C

Dry, citrus, almost nothing like what you expect Port to be. The locals drink it long, over ice with tonic and a strip of lemon.

Almonds, olives
02

Rosé

Rosado Cold, 6 °C

Invented in 2008 and still argued about. Strawberry, light, unserious in the best way.

Ice and a terrace
03

Ruby

Ruby Cool, 14 °C

Young and opaque. Aged in steel instead of wood, so it never oxidises and never loses that purple-red.

Blue cheese
04

LBV

Late Bottled Vintage Cool, 16 °C

One single harvest, four to six years in wood. Vintage character without the Vintage price or the waiting.

Dark chocolate
05

Tawny 10

Tawny 10 anos Cool, 14 °C

Oxidised deliberately, for a decade. Caramel, walnut, dried fig — and it goes amber at the rim as it ages.

Crème brûlée
06

Vintage

Vintage Room, 18 °C

One exceptional harvest, declared maybe three times a decade. Decant it hours ahead. Then stop talking.

Nothing. Just sit.
